Testimony Presenting LD 2028:

"Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in West Forks Plantation and The Forks Plantation the Gordon
Clifton Berry, Sr. Bridge"

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the Transportation Committee,
My name is Elizabeth Caruso. I live in Caratunk, which is part of the Greater Forks Area, and I represent the people of House District 72. I am honored to present to you LD 2028, "Resolve, to
Rename a Bridge in West Forks Plantation and The Forks Plantation the Gordon Clifton Berry,
Sr. Bridge" .
It is truly a deep privilege for me to stand here before you in honor of Gordon Berry Sr. Gordon was the steadfast pillar of our Forks Area community. He was an amazing husband, father, entrepreneur, and friend and loved by all who knew him... and he knew a lot of people from all
over Maine and the country.
Born in Jackman in 1954, Gordon passed away at his West Forks home on July 29, 2025 at the age of 70. He loved fishing, hunting, wildlife, giving his time to the community, and exploring the woods. At only 10 years old, Gordon began working at his parents' Berry's General Store, when it opened in the early 60's, and he worked until his last day. He graduated from Bingham's
Valley high school in 1973. He was married in 1979 to Carol, his precious wife of 46 years. He
became a father to Gordon Jr in 1982 and Brandon in 1987. A kind and compassionate person,
he was lauded as a great friend, a role model and leader to our community.
I've submitted his obituary for your review, but I wanted to highlight the following:
"Gordon was a simple man with a generous heart who believed deeply in making sure everyone had what they needed. He worked tirelessly at the family store -- seven days a week -- until his very last day. His dedication to both work and community was
unwavering. For over 40 years, he served on the volunteer Fire Department in West
Forks. He also took immense pride in founding the local deer feed program nearly 30
years ago -- a cause that reflected both his love for wildlife and commitment to giving back."
I met Gordon in 1992 when I became a Maine guide and would soon after own 3 businesses just `A1 mile from Berry's General Store. Gordon would greet me and others from behind the counter

with his genuine warmth and kindness, joy, and acceptance. He was a ready source of wisdom and good 01' Maine common sense as well as a wealth of local knowledge and history of the
area, geography and aspects of significance. His input in local decision-making was always critical and sought after.

I would like to highlight two aspects of Gordon's life.

Firstly, Gordon was a family man and a man of utmost character. He was steadfast, loving, and sacrificial in the way he cared for his family. The signature love of this family is shown by their
close-knit lives - working together in their family business in their family town. That is the unconditional love and acceptance that Carol and Gordon have always stewarded so deeply and that kept their sons closeby. That doesn't happen by accident - it is the purposeful and wellpracticed unconditional love and acceptance of amazing parents.

Secondly, Gordon's heart for people and the Forks Area community is what brought over I000 people to his service. Being a West Forks resident and business owner, I was in Berry's Store
quite frequently. It was the epitome of a Maine general store and local meeting place of the
young and old - the only store and gas station for 50 miles. Many times, I teased our guests and
clients, "if Berry's doesn't have it, you don't need it!"

Working closely with the snowmobile clubs, Gordon was always there to contribute and pitch in to the collaborative efforts of The Forks Area business economy. Whether it's building
snowmobile bridges, working on trails, contributing to the crews who are doing the work,
Gordon was there. . .always an integral voice and partner.

I vividly remember the days when the white-water industry was booming with a plethora of
rafting companies and guides. A significant majority had charge accounts at the store. They
would come in filling up buses, trip trucks, owners' vehicles, and then sign for their gas, food, or whatever other supplies they needed that day. Don't you know that Gordon Berry carried our tourism industry every month? Not some big bank, not some big corporation, but Gordon canied
us along until we paid the Berry's bill the following month.

In summary, Gordon prioritized family first and then community. Gordon Beny's store was the

pillar of the Forks area, and Gordon was at the center - the steadfast heartbeat of Beny's Store

E and our community. I feel it's only fitting that naming this bridge after Gordon will allow him to

still welcome people and to

our community!

Thank you for the opportunity to present this bill, and I respectfully urge the committee's support. I'd be happy to answer any questions.

Respectfully,

Rep. Elizabeth M. Caruso House District 72

Gordon Clifton Berry Sr.
WEST FORKS - Gordon Clifton Berry Sr., 70. of West Forks, passed away on July 29, 2025, in the town he called home for his entire life.
Bom on Oct. 28, 1954, in Jackman, Gordon was the son of Guy Clifton Berry and Francine Berry. He graduated from Upper Kennebec Valley High School and went on to build a life rooted in family,
hard work, and service to his community.
in 1979, Gordon married Carol, and together they raised their family in West Forks. A devoted husband and father, Gordon is survived by his wife Carol; his sons Gordon Berry Jr. and his wife Oi'll
Berry. and Brandon Beny and his wife Jillian Berry; his daughter Natasha Robinson; his sister Darlene Robinson; and grandsons Aisoon Suthinruek and Gabe Pooler.
He was predeceased by his parents; his brothers, Michael Berry, Jefirey Berry, and Ronnie Berry; and his sister Linda Robinson. Gordon was a simple man with a generous heart who believed deeply in making sure everyone had what they needed. He worked tirelessly at the family store - seven clays a week - until his very last day. His dedication to both work and community was unwavering. For over 40 years, he sewed on the volunteer Fire Department in West Forks. He also took immense pride in founding the local deer feed program nearly 30 years ago -- a cause that reflected both his love for wildlife and commitment to giving hack.
An outdoorsman through and through, Gordon found joy in hunting, fishing, trapping, snowmobiling, gold panning, collecting coins, and searching for deer and moose antlers. in earlier years he competed as a canoe racer. He loved spending time at l-Tish Pond camps with family or at"The River Camp" during hunting season. Whether cooking up meals to ensure no one_went hungry or playing a game of pool with friends, Gordon brought wannth and camaraderie wherever he went. One of Gordon's favorite past times, was watching Gunsmoke with his wife in the comfort of his
home.

Sunday Aug. 24, 2025, at 4 p.m., at the ballfieid in West Forks. Following the service, we wfll have food and solt drinks. The family invites attendees to wear casual attire - Berry's shirts and hats are especially welcome - as we gatherto honor a man who gave so much to this community.

Jeff McCabe Skowhegan LD 2028
My name is Jeff McCabe, and I am a resident of Skowhegan. I submit this testimony in support of the LD 2028 Resolve to rename a bridge in West Forks Plantation and The Forks Plantation the Gordon Clifton Berry, Sr. Bridge. I offer this testimony as a citizen of the State of Maine, a friend of the Berry family, and not in any official state capacity.
I have had the honor and privilege of knowing the Berry family for more than 25 years, and I admire them for many reasons. When I think about how to describe them, words like hard-working, kind, caring, friendly, resourceful, generous, and welcoming come to mind. My first visit to Berry's Store was in the late 1990s, and to this day I still get excited every time I walk through that door, whether I need anything or not.
Unfortunately, my work prevents me from being able to testify in person today, and I wish I could be there to hear the stories being shared. I want to thank the bill sponsor for submitting this resolve, as I know she and her family have strong ties to the Berry family and to Gordon. I also want to thank the Berry family for all that you do and for the hard work you continue to put into your community.
I have worked seasonally in the Upper Kennebec Valley for over two decades, and during that time I have witnessed the Berry family support the community in countless ways--through their time, financial support, and generosity. When I attended Gordon's memorial services and heard the stories shared, it became clear that what I had long suspected was true. Gordon supported people and businesses both larger and smaller than his own, simply because he was a good human being who genuinely cared about his community.
To me, Gordon remains larger than life. He was an avid outdoorsman, and his knowledge of the woods was legendary. Over the years, I have known of many acts of kindness carried out by Gordon--not because he sought recognition, but because others felt compelled to share how his generosity had impacted them.
Renaming this bridge is a well-deserved tribute to a great Mainer and a great human being. It is also a fitting recognition of Gordon's family, who continue his legacy of hard work and community support. Our state is a better place because of Gordon, and many of us are better people for having crossed paths with him.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I wish you all the best in the New Year.
Sincerely, Jeff McCabe Skowhegan

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at
MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 2028.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 2841.
Thank you.

Testimony of Senator Russell Black In Support of L.D. 2028, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in West Forks Plantation and The
Forks Plantation the Gordon Clifton Berry, Sr. Bridge Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
January 8, 2026
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation: my name is Russell Black, and I represent the people of Senate District 5. I am before you today in support of L.D. 2028, "Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in West Forks Plantation and The Forks Plantation the Gordon Clifton Berry, Sr. Bridge."
I am very happy to be a co-sponsor on this legislation alongside Representative Caruso to recognize the life of Gordon Clifton Berry, Sr., a man whose entire life was dedicated to this region and the people who live there.
In small, rural communities like West Forks, there are people who quietly become part of the backbone of the town. Gordon Berry was one of those people. He spent his life working, volunteering, and showing up for others without seeking recognition. For decades, he ran the family store, which served not just as a business, but as a gathering place and a lifeline for both locals and visitors. He was also a member of the West Forks Volunteer Fire Department for more than forty years, responding to emergencies and serving his neighbors whenever he was needed.
Gordon's commitment to his community went beyond his job and his uniform. He founded the local deer feed program nearly thirty years ago, and he remained deeply involved in the outdoor and sporting life of the region. He represented the values that define this part of Maine: hard work, self-reliance, generosity, and a deep connection to place.
This resolve seeks to name a bridge in West Forks Plantation and The Forks Plantation in Gordon Berry's honor. A bridge is an appropriate and meaningful tribute. It is something that quietly serves the public every day. It supports work, travel, emergency response, and community life. That kind of steady, dependable presence reflects the way Gordon lived.
Renaming this bridge as the Gordon Clifton Berry, Sr. Bridge would permanently recognize a man who devoted his life to the wellbeing of his community and would ensure that his legacy remains part of the region he never stopped serving.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
